title: Smooth affine toric algebras reduce to saturated sharp monoids and units
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $P$ a fine commutative monoid with torsion-free group completion $G$ [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. Assume that $\operatorname{Spec}k[P]\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth [def-trf-monoscheme-toric-realization] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Then $P=P^{\rm sat}$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k[P]$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Put $U=P^\times$ and $R=P/U$. The monoid $R$ is fine, saturated and sharp, its group completion is the finite free group $G/U$, and $U\simeq\mathbf Z^t$ for a finite $t\geq0$. There exists a monoid section $s:R\to P$ of the quotient such that $(q,u)\mapsto s(q)+u$ is an isomorphism $R\oplus U\simeq P$. Hence $k[P]\simeq k[R][y_1^{\pm1},\ldots,y_t^{\pm1}]$, and every localization of this ring at a prime ideal is regular local. In particular this applies to the maximal ideal generated by $e^q$ for $q\in R\setminus\{0\}$ and by $y_j-1$, whose residue field is $k$.

proof.text: Apply the existing affine monoid algebra normalization theorem. It gives that k[P] and k[G] are domains, the injective map k[G] into its fraction field K, the fraction-ring structure of K over k[P], and the characterization of integral elements as the image of k[P^sat]. This replaces the separate leading-term and integral-monomial constructions.

proof.text: Regularity gives integral closedness of every stalk, hence of every maximal localization via Spec.stalkIso. Apply local-to-global integral closedness to k[P]. If g has a positive power in P, it is in P^sat. Its single monomial in the saturated algebra maps to an element of K integral over k[P] by normalization. Integral closedness writes that element as an element a of k[P]. Injectivity of k[G] into K identifies the image of a with the single monomial e^g in k[G]. If g were outside the image of P, the coefficient of the image of a at g would be zero, while the coefficient of e^g is one. Thus g lies in P. Taking the submonoid closure of these positive roots gives P^sat=P.

proof.text: Convert this saturation equality, finite generation and injectivity into IsFineSaturatedMonoid P. Apply integral_sharpening_group_exactness to obtain the surjective canonical map pi:G->H=(Associates P)^gp, its unit kernel U, and injectivity of Associates P into H. The carrier description of U shows that it equals toricUnitSubgroup P, the subgroup closure of the images of units.

proof.text: The quotient monoid R=Associates P is finitely generated by surjectivity of P->R. For g in H with g^n=of(q), choose p in P representing q and x in G with pi(x)=g. Then pi(x^n/of(p))=1, so x^n/of(p)=of(u) for a unit u of P. Consequently x^n=of(p*u), and saturation of P gives x=of(r). Therefore g=of([r]), proving saturation of R. Its injectivity is supplied by exactness; its sharpness is Associates.isUnit_iff_eq_one.

source.place: VIII proof of Lemma 3.2.12(ii), p.104: saturation via finite normalization, then splitting off the unit group; section argument expanded by an agent.

proof.text: If g^n=1 in H for n>0, saturation of R puts both g and g^-1 in R. Injectivity of R->H makes their representatives multiply to one, so sharpness makes g=1. Thus H is torsion-free. Its finite generation follows from that of R and the finite-generation theorem for group completion. Apply the finite torsion-free Z-module basis theorem to H. The first isomorphism theorem for pi, with its kernel identified in step 4, gives the canonical equivalence H~=G/U; on every generator it sends of([p]) to the class of of(p). Composing its inverse with basis coordinates identifies G/U with a finite integer lattice.

proof.text: Apply fine_monoid_unit_splitting to P: the original completion is torsion-free by hypothesis and the sharp completion is torsion-free by step 6. Its stated conclusion supplies t, the unit lattice equivalence eU, a monoid section s of P->R, and the product equivalence eP with eP(q,u)=s(q)*u.

proof.text: Compose eP^-1 with the product of the identity on R and eU, then swap factors. MonoidAlgebra.domCongr followed by MonoidAlgebra.curryAlgEquiv gives the algebra equivalence eA:k[P]~=k[R][Z^t]. Their single-monomial formulas give exactly eA(e^(s(q)*u))=single(eU(u),e^q).

proof.text: For each prime of the Laurent algebra, pull it back along eA. Spec.stalkIso gives a regular localization of k[P] at that prime by step 1. Localization.localRingEquiv transports it along eA to the requested regular local Laurent localization.

proof.text: Define R->k by sending 1 to 1 and every other element to zero. If a*b=1 then a and b are units and hence identities, so sharpness proves multiplicativity. Extend it to k[R] by the monoid-algebra lift, and compose with the Laurent augmentation sending every group monomial to one. This k-algebra map kills the displayed vertex generators, so descends to the specified quotient. In that quotient each sharp nonidentity monomial is zero. The exponents whose Laurent monomials equal one form a subgroup containing each standard integer basis vector, since y_j-1 is a generator of the ideal. Each exponent is a product of integer powers of these basis vectors, so every Laurent monomial is one. Induction on the finite sums defining both monoid algebras now puts every quotient element in the image of k. The descended augmentation is a left inverse on k, so this scalar map is bijective. Its inverse is the specified quotient algebra equivalence with k; since the quotient is a field the ideal is maximal. Empty supports and empty bases use the same finite-sum and product identities.

lean.statement: theorem smooth_toric_saturated_sharp_reduction (k P : Type u) [Field k] [CommMonoid P] (hP : FineFan.IsFine P) (hG : ∀ (g : Algebra.GrothendieckGroup P) (n : ℕ), 0 < n → g ^ n = 1 → g = 1) (hSmooth : Smooth (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k (MonoidAlgebra k P))))) : FineFan.saturation (MonoidHom.mrange (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup.of (M := P))) = (MonoidHom.mrange (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup.of (M := P))) ∧ IsRegularScheme (Spec (.of (MonoidAlgebra k P))) ∧ IsFineSaturatedMonoid (Associates P) ∧ FineFan.IsSharp (Associates P) ∧ (∃ e : Algebra.GrothendieckGroup (Associates P) ≃* (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup P ⧸ toricUnitSubgroup P), ∀ p : P, e (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup.of (Associates.mk p)) = QuotientGroup.mk' (toricUnitSubgroup P) (Algebra.GrothendieckGroup.of p)) ∧ (∃ r : ℕ, Nonempty ((Algebra.GrothendieckGroup P ⧸ toricUnitSubgroup P) ≃* Multiplicative (Fin r → ℤ))) ∧ ∃ (t : ℕ) (eU : Pˣ ≃* Multiplicative (Fin t → ℤ)) (s : Associates P →* P) (eP : (Associates P × Pˣ) ≃* P) (eA : MonoidAlgebra k P ≃ₐ[k] toricLaurentAlgebra k (Associates P) t), (∀ q : Associates P, Associates.mk (s q) = q) ∧ (∀ (q : Associates P) (u : Pˣ), eP (q, u) = s q * (u : P)) ∧ (∀ (q : Associates P) (u : Pˣ), eA (MonoidAlgebra.of k P (s q * (u : P))) = MonoidAlgebra.single (eU u) (MonoidAlgebra.of k (Associates P) q)) ∧ (∀ (p : Ideal (toricLaurentAlgebra k (Associates P) t)) [p.IsPrime], IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime p)) ∧ (toricLaurentVertexIdeal k (Associates P) t).IsMaximal ∧ Nonempty ((toricLaurentAlgebra k (Associates P) t ⧸ toricLaurentVertexIdeal k (Associates P) t) ≃ₐ[k] k)
